items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: the leader of the regular orchestra or house band was named Vernon Andrade. Most every musician in New York worked for Vernon at one time or another

ctx.x: For the Arabian Night and the South Sea balls, all the employees which included the hostess and musicians, wore special costumes. We were dressed like Arabs and the hostess' like harem girls for Arabian night. For the South Sea Island ball we were in pirate costumes and the hostess' in Hawaiian straw dresses. For the Sissie's ball we were in our regular costumes to show at least there were a few men there.

Another well known dance hall at 7th Avenue and 138th Street was called the Renaissance. It was not as large as the Savoy but was very nice with a large balcony around three sides of the walls and one big bandstand. Usually private balls were held there and the leader of the regular orchestra or house band was named Vernon Andrade. Most every musician in New York worked for Vernon at one time or another because Vernon did not have a regular bunch of musicians that worked with him. As the Renaissance was not open…

Another place smaller than the Renaissance was the Bamboo which had a band under the leadership of Joe Steel, a fine pianist. And Chick Webb whom I had not met but had heard much talk about, was leading a band at a white dancing school on 125th Street and 7th Avenue which included a trumpeter named Bobby Starke whom I had met at the Rhythm Club.
